title: What If the Sun Sent You a Bill?
request: i have a script of about 3 minute long videos can i send it to you and see the final product
sources: Wikipedia, "Solar energy": the Earth receives 174 petawatts of sunlight at the top of the atmosphere, about 30 percent of which is reflected back to space. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solar_energy

US Energy Information Administration, Short-Term Energy Outlook: average US residential electricity price of 17.3 cents per kilowatt-hour in 2025 and a projected 18.2 cents in 2026. https://www.eia.gov/outlooks/steo/report/elec_coal_renew.php

Wikipedia, "List of countries by GDP (nominal)", IMF 2026 forecasts: United States about 32.4 trillion dollars, world about 126.3 trillion dollars. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_countries_by_GDP_(nominal)
Wikipedia, "World population": about 8.3 billion people in 2026. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_population
Wikipedia, "Sun": luminosity of 3.828 x 10^26 watts, about 4 billion kilograms of matter converted to energy each second. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sun
NASA, Sun facts: about 4.5 billion years old, with about 5 billion years left. https://science.nasa.gov/sun/facts/
US Energy Information Administration, Coal explained: coal holds energy stored by plants that lived hundreds of millions of years ago. https://www.eia.gov/energyexplained/coal/

US Energy Information Administration, Sources of energy: wind comes from uneven heating by the Sun, and geothermal and nuclear energy do not come from the Sun. https://www.eia.gov/energyexplained/what-is-energy/sources-of-energy.php

meter.label: Sunlight delivered since you pressed play

lines.speaker: host
lines.text: An envelope slides under your door.

lines.speaker: host
lines.text: No stamp. It is warm.

lines.speaker: host
lines.text: Inside is a bill, and the name at the top is yours.

lines.speaker: host
lines.text: Sender: the *Sun.*

lines.speaker: host
lines.text: Amount due, for the last hour of sunlight on Earth: thirty *trillion* dollars.

shots.words: An envelope slides under your door.

overlay.text: What If the Sun Sent You a Bill?

shots.words: No stamp. It is warm.
Inside is a bill, and the name at the top is yours.
Sender: the *Sun.*
Amount due, for the last hour of sunlight on Earth:
thirty *trillion* dollars.

lines.speaker: host
lines.text: You laugh. Then you check the sum.

lines.speaker: host
lines.text: Take all the sunlight that lands on this planet in one *hour.*

lines.speaker: host
lines.text: Price it like the electricity in your wall.

lines.speaker: host
lines.text: Thirty trillion. About what the whole United States earns in a year.

lines.speaker: host
lines.text: Every *four* hours, the Sun delivers the value of everything the entire world earns in a year.

lines.speaker: host
lines.text: And then it does it again.

shots.words: You laugh. Then you check the sum.
Take all the sunlight that lands on
this planet in one *hour.*
Price it like the electricity in your wall.
Thirty trillion. About what the whole United
States earns in a year.
Every *four* hours, the Sun delivers the value of
everything the entire world earns in a year.
And then it does it again.

lines.speaker: host
lines.text: In under ninety minutes, the Earth soaks up more energy than every city, car and factory will use this year.

shots.words: In under ninety minutes, the Earth soaks up
more energy than every city, car and factory
will use this year.

overlay.text: More than a whole year of it

lines.speaker: host
lines.text: You try the obvious defence. That is not all mine.

lines.speaker: host
lines.text: Fine. Split it between every person alive.

lines.speaker: host
lines.text: Your share is more than three thousand dollars. An hour.

lines.speaker: host
lines.text: Thirty *million* dollars a year, delivered to you, for free, since the day you were born.

shots.words: You try the obvious defence. That is not all mine.
Fine. Split it between every person alive.
Your share is more than three thousand dollars. An hour.
Thirty *million* dollars a year, delivered to you, for free,
since the day you were born.

lines.speaker: host
lines.text: Then you look at your real bills. Electricity. Fuel. Food.

lines.speaker: host
lines.text: And you notice something.

lines.speaker: host
lines.text: Coal is sunlight that plants caught hundreds of millions of years ago.

lines.speaker: host
lines.text: Oil is the same story.

shots.words: Then you look at your real bills. Electricity. Fuel. Food.
And you notice something.
Coal is sunlight that plants caught hundreds
of millions of years ago.
Oil is the same story.

lines.speaker: host
lines.text: Wind is air the Sun warmed. Rain is water the Sun lifted.

shots.words: Wind is air the Sun warmed.
Rain is water the Sun lifted.

lines.speaker: host
lines.text: Your dinner is this summer's light.

lines.speaker: host
lines.text: You have almost never paid for energy.

lines.speaker: host
lines.text: You have only paid for *delivery.*

shots.words: Your dinner is this summer's light.
You have almost never paid for energy.
You have only paid for *delivery.*

lines.speaker: host
lines.text: And the coal and the oil? That is a *savings* account.

shots.words: And the coal and the oil?
That is a *savings* account.

lines.speaker: host
lines.text: Sunlight, deposited a little at a time, over hundreds of millions of years.

lines.speaker: host
lines.text: We found the account a few hundred years ago.

lines.speaker: host
lines.text: We have been emptying it ever since.

shots.words: Sunlight, deposited a little at a time,
over hundreds of millions of years.

overlay.text: Hundreds of millions of years later

shots.words: We found the account a few hundred years ago.
We have been emptying it ever since.

lines.speaker: host
lines.text: So you turn the bill over, looking for the catch.

lines.speaker: host
lines.text: There is a second page. It shows what this costs the sender.

shots.words: So you turn the bill over, looking for the catch.
There is a second page.
It shows what this costs the sender.

lines.speaker: host
lines.text: Every second, the Sun destroys four million *tonnes* of itself to make that light.

lines.speaker: host
lines.text: And Earth catches almost none of it. One part in two billion.

lines.speaker: host
lines.text: The rest pours into empty space, unbilled, unseen, for *nobody.*

shots.words: Every second, the Sun destroys four million *tonnes*
of itself to make that light.
And Earth catches almost none of it.
One part in two billion.
The rest pours into empty space, unbilled,
unseen, for *nobody.*

lines.speaker: host
lines.text: It has done this for four and a half billion years.

shots.words: It has done this for four and a half billion years.

lines.speaker: host
lines.text: Before your street. Before people.

shots.words: Before your street. Before people.

lines.speaker: host
lines.text: Before anything alive could look up.

shots.words: Before anything alive could look up.

lines.speaker: host
lines.text: It lit oceans with nothing in them.

shots.words: It lit oceans with nothing in them.

lines.speaker: host
lines.text: No *invoice.* No reminder. No *interest.*

shots.words: No *invoice.* No reminder. No *interest.*

lines.speaker: host
lines.text: At the bottom there is one last line, and it is not a demand.

lines.speaker: host
lines.text: Amount due: nothing.

lines.speaker: host
lines.text: It was never a bill. It was a statement.

lines.speaker: host
lines.text: *Paid* in full, by the sender.

lines.speaker: host
lines.text: Remaining credit: about five billion years.

lines.speaker: host
lines.text: You fold it up. Outside, it is morning.

lines.speaker: host
lines.text: And for the first time in your life, you feel the Sun on your face and know exactly what it is *worth.*
